value.markup:
crombolo users disable

Stop a user signing in, and end their sessions. Safe to run again: a second run changes nothing more.

crombolo users disable <user>
ArgumentWhat it is
userTheir e-mail address or username. Required.

crombolo users enable

Let a disabled user sign in again. Safe to run again: a second run changes nothing more.

crombolo users enable <user>
ArgumentWhat it is
userTheir e-mail address or username. Required.

crombolo users groups export

Make a group made in the back office one of the site's own. Safe to run again: a second run changes nothing more.

crombolo users groups export <alias> [--dry-run] [--no-apply]
ArgumentWhat it is
aliasThe group's alias. Required.
--dry-runSay what would change, and change nothing.
--no-applyChange it, and leave applying it to `crombolo types sync`.

crombolo users groups list

The user groups: the site's own, and those made in the back office. Changes nothing.

crombolo users groups list

crombolo users groups new

Add a user group of the site's own. Safe to run again: a second run changes nothing more.

crombolo users groups new <alias> --name <name> [--description <description>] [--icon <icon>] [--section <section>] [--permission <permission>] [--language <language>] [--dry-run] [--no-apply]
ArgumentWhat it is
aliasThe group's alias. Required.
--nameIts name. Required.
--descriptionIts description.
--iconIts icon.
--sectionA section it may open; give each.
--permissionA permission it holds; give each.
--languageA language it may edit, or all; give each.
--dry-runSay what would change, and change nothing.
--no-applyChange it, and leave applying it to `crombolo types sync`.

crombolo users groups permissions

The permissions a user group can hold, and what each allows. Changes nothing.

crombolo users groups permissions [--verbs]
ArgumentWhat it is
--verbsShow the name each is kept under as well.

crombolo users groups remove

Remove a user group, moving its users to another. Safe to run again: a second run changes nothing more.

crombolo users groups remove <alias> [--move-users-to <move-users-to>] [--dry-run] [--no-apply]
ArgumentWhat it is
aliasThe group's alias. Required.
--move-users-toThe group its users move to.
--dry-runSay what would change, and change nothing.
--no-applyChange it, and leave the database as it is.

crombolo users groups sections

The sections a user group may open, and what each holds. Changes nothing.

crombolo users groups sections

crombolo users groups show

One user group: its sections, permissions and languages. Changes nothing.

crombolo users groups show <alias>
ArgumentWhat it is
aliasThe group's alias. Required.

crombolo users groups update

Change a user group's name, sections, permissions or languages. Safe to run again: a second run changes nothing more.

crombolo users groups update <alias> [--name <name>] [--description <description>] [--icon <icon>] [--section <section>] [--remove-section <remove-section>] [--permission <permission>] [--remove-permission <remove-permission>] [--all-languages] [--language <language>] [--remove-language <remove-language>] [--dry-run] [--no-apply]
ArgumentWhat it is
aliasThe group's alias. Required.
--nameIts name.
--descriptionIts description; "" for none.
--iconIts icon.
--sectionA section it may open.
--remove-sectionA section it may no longer open.
--permissionA permission it holds.
--remove-permissionA permission it no longer holds.
--all-languagesIt may edit every language.
--languageA language it may edit.
--remove-languageA language it may no longer edit.
--dry-runSay what would change, and change nothing.
--no-applyChange it, and leave applying it to `crombolo types sync`.

crombolo users invite

Create a user and print the link they set their password with. Each run acts again.

crombolo users invite <email> [--group <group>] [--name <name>]
ArgumentWhat it is
emailTheir e-mail address. Required.
--groupA user group, by alias; repeatable.
--nameTheir name; the address when not given.

crombolo users list

The back-office users: who, their groups, their state and last sign-in. Changes nothing.

crombolo users list [--limit <limit>] [--offset <offset>] [--fields <fields>]
ArgumentWhat it is
--limitHow many to list. Default 50.
--offsetHow many to skip first. Default 0.
--fieldsOnly these fields of each item, comma-separated.

crombolo users reset-2fa

Remove a user's second factors, so their next sign-in sets one up again. Safe to run again: a second run changes nothing more.

crombolo users reset-2fa <user>
ArgumentWhat it is
userTheir e-mail address or username. Required.

crombolo users reset-password

Give a user a new password, and end their sessions. Each run acts again.

crombolo users reset-password <user> [--stdin]
ArgumentWhat it is
userTheir e-mail address or username. Required.
--stdinRead the new password from stdin.

crombolo users unlock

Clear a user's lockout and failed sign-ins. Safe to run again: a second run changes nothing more.

crombolo users unlock <user>
ArgumentWhat it is
userTheir e-mail address or username. Required.

crombolo admin reset-password

Reset the administrator's password and print it. Each run acts again.

crombolo admin reset-password [--stdin]
ArgumentWhat it is
--stdinRead the new password from stdin.

crombolo api-client rotate

Issue a new secret for the API client, and print it once. Each run acts again.

crombolo api-client rotate [--client <client>]
ArgumentWhat it is
--clientThe client id; CROMBOLO_API_CLIENT_ID when not given.

crombolo audit list

The audit log, newest first, a page at a time. Changes nothing.

crombolo audit list [--since <since>] [--until <until>] [--user <user>] [--category <category>] [--action <action>] [--entity <entity>] [--remote <remote>] [--env <env>] [--limit <limit>] [--before <before>]
ArgumentWhat it is
--sinceEntries at or after this time.
--untilEntries before this time.
--userOne person, by e-mail, login or key; a login with no account finds its failed sign-ins.
--categoryOne kind of change. One of content, media, member, schema, settings, user, permission, sign-in, system.
--actionOne action, such as Publish or SignIn.
--entityWhat one item had done to it.
--remoteRead a hosted site through this remote, signed in as you.
--envThe remote's environment.
--limitHow many on a page. Default 50.
--beforeThe page after this cursor.

crombolo audit stream

The audit log as NDJSON, oldest first; --follow keeps it coming. Changes nothing.

crombolo audit stream [--since <since>] [--until <until>] [--user <user>] [--category <category>] [--action <action>] [--entity <entity>] [--remote <remote>] [--env <env>] [--after <after>] [--follow] [--interval <interval>]
ArgumentWhat it is
--sinceEntries at or after this time.
--untilEntries before this time.
--userOne person, by e-mail, login or key; a login with no account finds its failed sign-ins.
--categoryOne kind of change. One of content, media, member, schema, settings, user, permission, sign-in, system.
--actionOne action, such as Publish or SignIn.
--entityWhat one item had done to it.
--remoteRead a hosted site through this remote, signed in as you.
--envThe remote's environment.
--afterCarry on after this entry id. Default 0.
--followKeep reading new entries until stopped.
--intervalSeconds between reads with --follow. Default 5.

values.value: the command line’s own description of its commands
Back office users, the administrator’s password, API clients and the audit log.
